author: Nayan Seth
description:
The US Congress on Wednesday passed a bill to strengthen sanctions on Russia by targeting Moscow’s leading energy buyers – China and India – just days before Chinese President Xi Jinping is due to arrive in Washington for a bilateral summit with President Donald Trump.
The US House of Representatives cleared the “Lindsey Graham Sanctioning Russia and Iran Act of 2026” by a 262-159 vote, making its way to the White House for Trump’s signature. The Senate passed the bill last month by an...
title: US Congress passes bill targeting Russia’s leading energy buyers – China and India

author: Mark Magnier
description:
The criminal trial of Huawei Technologies on racketeering charges shifted this week into a slower, more laborious pace in what is expected to be a weeks-long trial as the US Government sought to establish on Wednesday that Huawei was intent on learning about a proprietary robot developed by US telecommunications carrier T-Mobile.
Matthew Skurnik, assistant US attorney for the Eastern District of New York, spent hours running FBI Special Agent James Diclemis through a series of emails that...
title: Huawei accused of stealing robot tech to get hands on T-Mobile’s trade secrets

author: Ling Xin
description:
China said it can now predict weather 10 days in advance at a cutting-edge resolution of 5km (3.1 miles), finer than most major systems in routine use around the world.
The advance was achieved by a Chinese-developed weather forecasting model running on Sugon 8,000, a massive home-grown computing system built entirely with domestically made AI chips.
Most major global forecasting systems have resolutions of roughly 5km to 10km, according to the China Meteorological Administration and...
title: China uses 100,000 home-grown AI chips to build leading weather forecast system

author: Shi Jiangtao
description:
In talks with his Iranian counterpart in Beijing on Wednesday, China’s foreign minister reaffirmed Beijing’s support for Tehran, called for a political settlement to the country’s conflict with the US and warned that regional tensions must not further spill over into Yemen.
Wang Yi also urged the earliest possible reopening of the Strait of Hormuz.
Abbas Araghchi’s trip to China, his second since the US launched large-scale strikes on Iran in late February, came as Washington expanded sanctions...
title: China affirms support for Iran, but warns against Yemen spillover

author: Amber Wang,Alcott Wei,Albee Zhang
description:
A plenary session at a Beijing security conference turned into a heated exchange on Wednesday, when a senior Iranian defence official and a Saudi think tank chief traded accusations over the conflict in the Middle East.
In the city where just a few years ago Iran and Saudi Arabia signed a peace deal, Prince Turki al-Faisal, chairman of the Saudi think tank the King Faisal Centre for Research and Islamic Studies, accused Iran of not respecting “the sovereignty of the Arab states”.
In a clear...
title: Iranian and Saudi panellists spar at Xiangshan Forum over Middle East attacks

author: Victoria Bela
description:
A former director of a state-owned museum at the centre of a rare high-profile art scandal was sentenced to three years in prison, Chinese state media said on Wednesday.
Xu Huping was found to have abused his position at the Nanjing Museum in eastern Jiangsu province and taken bribes, including money and property, for helping others secure projects and business collaborations.
He was sentenced to prison for three years and fined 200,000 yuan (US$29,800), according to state news agency...
title: Former director of leading Chinese museum jailed 3 years after art-selling scandal

author: Dewey Sim,Amber Wang,Alcott Wei,Albee Zhang
description:
With just a week to go until Chinese President Xi Jinping heads to Washington for his first state visit in more than a decade, Chinese Defence Minister Dong Jun opted for the diplomatic path in his address to China’s premier security conference on Wednesday.
Speaking at the annual Xiangshan Forum in Beijing, Dong took veiled swipes at Washington and its allies but – unlike last year – appeared to pull his punches, skipping mentions of contentious issues such as Taiwan and the South China Sea.
He...
title: Chinese defence chief skirts flashpoints at Xiangshan Forum ahead of Xi-Trump summit

author: William Zheng
description:
The United Nations can count on China’s support, the UN’s peacekeeping chief said in Beijing as he flagged the body’s financial strains – due in large part to Washington’s funding squeeze.
Speaking at the Xiangshan Forum in Beijing on Wednesday, UN undersecretary general for peace operations Jean-Pierre Lacroix said the international system was under severe strain and the UN urgently needed to adapt its tools to modern realities.
Lacroix warned that the global body’s financial situation “is...
title: As US slashes funding, UN peacekeeping head says global body can rely on China

author: Carol Yang
description:
A US military honour guard held a rehearsal at the White House as Washington fine-tuned diplomatic protocols and preparations for Chinese President Xi Jinping’s expected visit to the United States next week.
A video clip posted on social media by Fox News correspondent Lucas Tomlinson on Tuesday afternoon Washington time showed service members from various military branches dressed in ceremonial uniform and standing in formation.
The drill mirrored the welcome extended to US President Donald...
title: US military prepares ceremonial welcome for Xi Jinping at the White House

author: Victoria Bela
description:
Geologists have discovered two large water sources beneath China’s largest desert, potentially offering the northwestern region a vital new tap for sand-control projects and agriculture.
The desert region has drawn attention for extensive afforestation and anti-desertification efforts taking place around its edges under the Great Green Wall initiative, alongside a rainfall trend that is transforming arid western China.
The groundwater discoveries were made as part of a water-finding project in...
title: Geologists find unexpectedly large water sources in Xinjiang beneath China’s largest desert

author: Meredith Chen
description:
China confirmed on Wednesday that a research vessel conducted a month-long, wide-ranging geological survey in the waters near Scarborough Shoal, a South China Sea flashpoint between Beijing and Manila.
The Haiyang Dizhi Shihao, or Marine Geology No 10, carried out the survey from August 11 to September 8, with the aim of “gaining a comprehensive understanding of the basic geological features and ecological environment” of waters under its jurisdiction, the Ministry of Natural Resources said on...
title: Chinese research ship completes month-long mission near Scarborough Shoal

author: Amber Wang,Albee Zhang
description:
China should use its maritime militia as an extra force to collect information and maintain a regular presence in the South China Sea, where it is coming into frequent conflict with the Philippines.
That was the suggestion Wu Shicun, the founding president of China’s National Institute for South China Sea Studies, made on Tuesday on the sidelines of the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, an annual defence gathering in the capital attended by security officials and researchers from nearly 100 countries...
title: Should Beijing use its maritime militia as a backup force in the South China Sea?

author: Ling Xin
description:
Chinese researchers have developed the world’s smallest CT scanner, a portable device designed to produce images of tiny fossils and archaeological relics.
Built by the Shandong province-based Rayim, the Xtomo-Cube is about the size of a desktop speaker and weighs just 6kg (13.2lbs).
“The device can be held in one hand and is the world’s smallest and lightest CT system, earning it the nickname ‘palm-sized CT scanner’,” Liu Baodong, a senior engineer at the Chinese Academy of Sciences and general...
title: Chinese scientists build world’s smallest CT scanner, weighing just 6kg

author: Alyssa Chen
description:
The leadership change in Okinawa could deal a quiet blow to Beijing’s attempts to leverage local opposition to remilitarisation and the US-Japan military alliance, according to analysts.
They added that the shift would compel Chinese academics and state media to recalibrate their messaging and approach towards the strategically vital Japanese prefecture.
Genta Koja, the 42-year-old backed by Japan’s ruling Liberal Democratic Party to become Okinawa’s new governor, defeated incumbent Denny Tamaki...
title: How will the Okinawa governor’s race result reshape China’s local messaging?

author: Dewey Sim
description:
Chinese Defence Minister Dong Jun’s address to a defence gathering in Beijing on Wednesday carried a message for Washington but it was delivered in a notably softer, less critical tone, according to a retired senior colonel in the People’s Liberation Army.
Zhou Bo, now a senior fellow at the Centre for International Security and Strategy at Tsinghua University, said Dong’s tone was “relatively mild”, even as the Chinese defence minister made veiled references to the US and its actions in the...
title: Dong Jun adopts softer stance on US at Xiangshan Forum as Xi prepares for Trump summit

author: Seong Hyeon Choi
description:
Chinese Defence Minister Dong Jun gave a keynote speech to the Xiangshan Forum in Beijing on Wednesday, with just over a week until a summit in the United States between the presidents of the two countries.
In his 20-minute address, Dong outlined China’s goals for global governance, multilateralism, conflict prevention and the development of emerging technology.
Global security at a ‘moment of fragility’
Dong started by warning that a “zero-sum mindset” could not resolve today’s problems.
He...
title: Fragility and cooperation: the takeaways from Dong Jun’s Xiangshan Forum speech

author: Ziang Liu
description:
The first “China shock” was fairly easy to understand. Beginning in the 1990s, cheap Chinese goods poured into global markets, displacing large parts of lower-end manufacturing across the world. Now, China shock 2.0 seems to be under way, with China taking the lead in electric vehicles (EVs), batteries, solar panels, semiconductors and other more technologically sophisticated industries.
This is often perceived as a trade problem, with Chinese manufacturers producing too much, selling too...
title: Neither tariffs nor export controls will stop China’s industrial engine

author: SCMP Reporters
description:

Beijing is hosting China’s most important annual defence conference, the Beijing Xiangshan Forum, bringing defence officials, former politicians and think tank experts to the city from around the world.
About 200 specialists and researchers are expected to take part in the forum this week, which many see as Beijing’s answer to Singapore’s annual Shangri-la Dialogue, the region’s biggest...
title: Defence chief Dong Jun at Xiangshan Forum: China willing to share military experience
